title: How to Store Cut Onion Safely

seo.title: How to Store Cut Onion Safely
seo.meta_description: A cut onion should be refrigerated because exposed surfaces become contaminated and lose quality faster than a whole onion.
seo.search_intent: Learn how to store cut onion safely with a practical, safe sequence that lets the reader act without an obvious second search.

excerpt: A cut onion should be refrigerated because exposed surfaces become contaminated and lose quality faster than a whole onion. Use a clean covered container, chill it promptly, and discard it if it has spent too long at room temperature or shows clear spoilage.
content_html:
A cut onion should be refrigerated because exposed surfaces become contaminated and lose quality faster than a whole onion. Use a clean covered container, chill it promptly, and discard it if it has spent too long at room temperature or shows clear spoilage.

Refrigerate cut onion promptly

Refrigerate cut onion at 40°F (4°C) or below within two hours of cutting, or within one hour when ambient temperature is above about 90°F (32°C). That clock includes preparation and serving time.

Use a clean covered container

Wrap the piece well or place it in a sealed container to limit contamination, drying, and odor transfer. Keep it separate from raw meat and other foods that can drip.

Quality declines even when refrigerated

Onion gradually loses firmness and aroma in the refrigerator. Use older pieces first and discard if mold, slime, or clearly abnormal odor appears; do not taste questionable food to judge safety.

Do not re-refrigerate onion left out too long

Putting it back in the refrigerator does not reset the safety clock. If cut onion remained out beyond recommended limits, discard it even if it still looks normal.

faq.question: How long can cut onion stay out at room temperature?
faq.answer: Refrigerate cut onion at 40°F (4°C) or below within two hours of cutting, or within one hour when ambient temperature is above about 90°F (32°C). That clock includes preparation and serving time.

faq.question: How should cut onion be stored in the refrigerator?
faq.answer: Wrap the piece well or place it in a sealed container to limit contamination, drying, and odor transfer. Keep it separate from raw meat and other foods that can drip.

faq.question: Can I refrigerate cut onion again after it sat out for several hours?
faq.answer: Putting it back in the refrigerator does not reset the safety clock. If cut onion remained out beyond recommended limits, discard it even if it still looks normal.
